newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close much stronger on job reports.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close much stronger on job reports.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Friday, matching sharp gains in U.S. Treasuries as investors were cheered by tame employment reports in both countries, analysts said.

"With the payroll numbers down south, although though headline number in terms of jobs created was a little bit higher than the consensus, underlying that were generally very positive things," said Michael Gregory, a fixed income economists and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$1.05 to C$111.65 to yield 7.021 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 20/32 to yield 6.71 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 31 basis points from 33 basis points at Thursday's close.

The U.S. non-farm payrolls report showed employment there grew by 271,000 jobs in January, above forecasts of a 237,000 increase. Analysts said the source of the bond rally was a portion of the report showing average hourly earnings rose less than expected.
The U.S. jobs report had a far greater impact on Canadian bonds than the Canadian report, which was released 90 minutes earlier.
The Canadian jobs report showed the Canada's unemployment rate was unchanged at 9.7 percent in January from December. Employment rose by by just 5,100 to 13.76 million.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast that Canada's unemployment rate will fall to 9.6 percent in January.
Long-term Canadian bonds continued to outperform short-term issues as many dealers placed curve flattening trades, analysts said.
The long end of the yield curve is also benefitting from renewed optimism about the potential for the spread between Canadian and U.S. long bonds yields to narrow, Gregory said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.60 to C$104.65 to yield 6.353 percent.
The U.S. bond rose 15/32 to yield 6.40 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was five basis points.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.82 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.12 percent.
